parsed.explanation: Documented criminalisation is enforced directly against visibly gender-nonconforming people, not a dead letter: trans women received 8- and 14-year sentences for same-sex sections and served in men's prisons, police arbitrarily arrest and assault trans people, impose forced stripping/medical exams, extort, and distribute photos. The 2024 constitutional court upheld 14-year offences with corporal punishment, senior officials frame trans/gay people as threats, hate-speech prosecution was discontinued, and no effective remedy is documented. This is recurring state targeting with severe custody consequences, below execution regimes but at the severe-risk level.

entry_documents.interaction: Border/document screening is unresolved, but arrest and custody exposure begins once identity is discovered through appearance or a same-sex-read relationship.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans women convicted under section 153 served 8 and 14 years in men's prisons; arrested people faced forced stripping, forced medical/HIV exams, extortion and photo distribution.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arbitrary arrest leads directly to birth-sex/men's custody and corporal-punishment-eligible offences, with no documented placement safeguard.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No generic bathroom rule is documented, but men's-prison placement after conviction is a birth-sex custodial exposure.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Criminalisation converts any police encounter into possible detention; private hospitality cannot override penal provisions applied against trans presentation.

care_services.exposure: Medical staff denied services on gender-expression grounds; a beaten trans man was refused treatment and nurses mocked people seeking HIV tests; forced exams also documented after arrest.
care_services.interaction: Seeking care can out a visitor and, in custody, becomes coercive examination rather than treatment.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Sections 153/154/156 upheld June 2024, carrying up to 14 years with corporal punishment; court left reform to legislature. Presidents, party and religious actors threaten or dehumanise gay/trans people; 2016 'kill' post prosecution was discontinued.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Moratorium announced 2012-2015 was annulled in 2016; police worked around it, e.g. charging under a different section in 2018.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing plus efficient courts enforcing the offences makes rule of law a liability, not recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans visitor travelling with a minor or partner read as same-sex has no relationship recognition; marriage law bans same-sex unions and assigns gender at birth. Arrest could separate family, but no minor-specific rule is sourced.
minors_guardians.interaction: Exposure is via adult criminalisation and custody, not a documented child-specific offence; do not infer a separate minor penalty.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2018 report based on 45 LGBT interviews: police arbitrarily arrested/detained trans people and sometimes assaulted them. Arrested men were ransacked, assaulted, threatened with burning alive, extorted by community police.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are perpetrators and extortion actors, so reporting violence exposes the victim to the same enforcement.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No effective remedy documented: constitutional challenge dismissed 2024, hate-speech case discontinued, moratorium annulled and circumvented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: 2019 broadcast hate-speech rule is media-specific for residents; its enforcement for visitors is not documented and does not offset penal exposure.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknown border practice and violence magnitude do not mitigate the documented custody and arrest regime.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: recurring police targeting for gender presentation, severe custody in men's facilities, courts enforcing hostile law, and failed complaints. This case has longer documented sentences (8-14 years) and corporal-punishment exposure, offset only slightly by less evidence of systematic street sweeps.

Lower than 0.25-A: that anchor has raids, extortion and days-long detention with sexual harassment but no routine pattern of torture. Here convictions run to years, corporal punishment is authorised, and forced medical examinations are documented.

Far lower than 0.45-A: that anchor is a universal bathroom exclusion without presentation arrests and with a prosecuted assault. Here criminalisation is actively used against trans women themselves, with police assault and no working remedy.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is criminalisation plus documented practice: gender-nonconforming appearance makes a visitor the most likely target, police arrest/assault/extort, courts impose years in men's prisons under offences carrying corporal punishment, and the 2024 court and discontinued hate prosecution show no recourse. Official and religious threat-framing legitimises this. Unknown border rules do not soften it, because discovery through appearance, documents, care-seeking or a same-sex-read companion triggers the same penal and custodial exposure for adults and travelling families.
